summary: This note covers the 1969–70 season of the American Hockey League, its 34th season. Nine teams each played 72 games. The Montreal Voyageurs, the league's second Canada-based team, finished first overall in the regular season, while the Buffalo Bisons won the Calder Cup and ended their AHL run as the NHL prepared to add the Buffalo Sabres.
one_line: The 1969–70 AHL season, the league's 34th, featuring nine teams, the Montreal Voyageurs' first-place finish, and the Buffalo Bisons' final Calder Cup title.
key_facts: The 1969–70 AHL season was the 34th season of the American Hockey League.
Nine teams played 72 games each in the season schedule.
The Montreal Voyageurs became the second Canada-based team in the American Hockey League.
The Montreal Voyageurs finished first overall in the regular season.
This was the last season for the Buffalo Bisons in the AHL.
The National Hockey League added the Buffalo Sabres, who began play the next season.
The Buffalo Bisons won their fifth Calder Cup championship in this season.
